name: Reign of Justinian
summary: The eastern emperor codified Roman law and briefly reconquered Italy, North Africa and southern Spain.
body:
The *Corpus Juris Civilis* is the foundation of civil law systems across Europe and Latin America today. His reconquest was undone by the [plague](event:justinian-plague) and by war exhaustion.

More at [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justinian_I).

name: Justinian's reconquest wars
summary: Justinian sent armies to reconquer the Roman west from the Vandal and Gothic kingdoms, recovering North Africa, Italy and part of southern Spain at great cost.
body:
Part of [Reign of Justinian](event:justinian). The Italian campaign alone lasted nearly twenty years and left the peninsula devastated; the [plague](event:justinian-plague) and renewed war with Persia drained the treasury, and most of the western gains were lost within a generation.

More at [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gothic_War_(535%E2%80%93554)).

name: Hagia Sophia completed
summary: The great domed church of Constantinople was the largest interior space in the world for nearly a thousand years.
body:
Part of [Reign of Justinian](event:justinian). The great domed church of Constantinople was the largest interior space in the world for nearly a thousand years.

More at [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hagia_Sophia).

name: Plague of Justinian
summary: The first recorded pandemic of bubonic plague killed perhaps 15–50 million people around the Mediterranean.
body:
Part of [Reign of Justinian](event:justinian). Caused by the same bacterium as the later [Black Death](event:black-death), it struck Constantinople at the height of Justinian's reconquest and helped ensure it did not last.

More at [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plague_of_Justinian).

name: Tang dynasty
summary: A cosmopolitan Chinese golden age of poetry, Buddhism and long-distance trade, with Chang'an the largest city on Earth.
body:
Li Bai and Du Fu wrote in this period; the imperial examination system matured; and [woodblock printing](event:woodblock-printing) appeared.

More at [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tang_dynasty).

name: The Hijra and the founding of Islam
summary: Muhammad and his followers migrated from Mecca to Medina, founding the first Muslim community; year one of the Islamic calendar.
body:
Within a decade the new faith had united the Arabian peninsula, and within a century its armies and merchants had carried it from Spain to the Indus in the [early Muslim conquests](event:islamic-conquests).

Islam is today the second largest religion in the world and shaped law, science and art across three continents.

More at [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hijrah).

name: Early Muslim conquests
summary: Arab armies took Persia, Egypt, the Levant, North Africa and Spain within roughly a century.
body:
Part of [The Hijra and the founding of Islam](event:hijra). The Sasanian empire was destroyed outright and Byzantium lost its richest provinces at [Yarmouk](event:yarmouk). The advance into Western Europe was checked at [Tours](event:tours) in 732.

More at [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Early_Muslim_conquests).

links.label: The Hijra and the founding of Islam

name: Battle of Yarmouk
summary: A decisive Arab victory over the Byzantine field army opened Syria and Palestine to Muslim rule.
body:
Part of [Early Muslim conquests](event:islamic-conquests). A decisive Arab victory over the Byzantine field army opened Syria and Palestine to Muslim rule.

More at [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_the_Yarmuk).

name: The Reconquista
summary: Christian kingdoms took the Iberian peninsula from Muslim rule over nearly eight centuries.
body:
It ended with the surrender of [Granada](event:granada) in January 1492, months before [Columbus](event:columbus) sailed with Castilian backing.

More at [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reconquista).

name: Battle of Tours
summary: Charles Martel's Franks halted an Umayyad raiding army between Tours and Poitiers.
body:
Part of [Early Muslim conquests](event:islamic-conquests). Charles Martel's Franks halted an Umayyad raiding army between Tours and Poitiers.

More at [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_Tours).

name: Harun al-Rashid's reign
summary: The Abbasid caliph presided over Baghdad at its height as a commercial and intellectual centre, patronising scholarship and exchanging embassies with distant powers.
body:
Part of [Islamic Golden Age](event:islamic-golden-age). Harun's court sponsored the translation of Greek and Persian works that his successors would gather into the House of Wisdom. The *Thousand and One Nights* later cast his reign as a legendary age of marvels.

More at [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harun_al-Rashid).

name: Islamic Golden Age
summary: Baghdad, Córdoba and Cairo became centres of mathematics, astronomy, medicine and philosophy.
body:
Greek, Persian and Indian works were translated into Arabic at the House of Wisdom, then extended: [algebra](event:al-khwarizmi), optics, the astrolabe, hospitals and pharmacology. Much of this learning re-entered Europe through Spain and Sicily.

More at [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Islamic_Golden_Age).

name: Viking Age
summary: Scandinavian raiders, traders and settlers ranged from Newfoundland to Baghdad for nearly three centuries.
body:
They sacked [Lindisfarne](event:lindisfarne), settled Iceland, Greenland and briefly [Vinland](event:vinland), founded Dublin and Kyiv, and conquered Normandy — from which their descendants took [England](event:hastings).

More at [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Viking_Age).

name: Raid on Lindisfarne
summary: The sack of the Northumbrian monastery is the conventional opening of the Viking Age in Europe.
body:
Part of [Viking Age](event:viking-age). The sack of the Northumbrian monastery is the conventional opening of the Viking Age in Europe.

More at [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lindisfarne).

name: Heian Period in Japan
summary: An age of refined aristocratic culture in Japan, producing some of the world's earliest novels and poetry, before the rise of the samurai.
body:
The Fujiwara regents ruled from Kyoto; the court produced *The Tale of Genji*, Japan's first great novel, and refined calligraphy and landscape art.

More at [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heian_period).

name: Charlemagne crowned emperor
summary: The pope crowned the Frankish king emperor in Rome, reviving an imperial title in the west after 324 years.
body:
Charlemagne's realm covered most of western Europe and its court sponsored a revival of learning and a legible new script. Its division among his grandsons sketched the outlines of France and Germany.

More at [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlemagne).

name: Al-Khwarizmi and algebra
summary: His treatise on balancing equations gave algebra its name, and a Latin garbling of his own gave us "algorithm".
body:
Part of [Islamic Golden Age](event:islamic-golden-age). His treatise on balancing equations gave algebra its name, and a Latin garbling of his own gave us "algorithm".

More at [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Al-Khwarizmi).

name: Invention of gunpowder
summary: Chinese alchemists seeking an elixir of immortality found a mixture that burned explosively.
body:
By the thirteenth century it was in bombs and rockets; carried west along the [Silk Road](event:silk-road), it produced the cannon that would eventually bring down [Constantinople](event:fall-constantinople) and the castle.

More at [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/History_of_gunpowder).

name: Woodblock printing
summary: The Diamond Sutra, printed in China in 868, is the oldest dated printed book that survives.
body:
Part of [Tang dynasty](event:tang-dynasty). The Diamond Sutra, printed in China in 868, is the oldest dated printed book that survives.

More at [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Woodblock_printing).

name: Fatimid Caliphate
summary: A rival Shiite caliphate ruling North Africa and Egypt, competing with the Abbasids for religious authority and territorial dominance.
body:
Founded in Ifriqiya and ruling from Cairo after 969, the Fatimids built a Shia counter-caliphate to the Sunni Abbasids and drew wealth from Red Sea trade. Saladin ended the dynasty in 1171 and returned Egypt to Abbasid allegiance.

More at [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fatimid_Caliphate).

name: Song Dynasty
summary: A high point of Chinese civilisation: landscape painting and poetry, printing and paper money, gunpowder weapons and a booming maritime commerce.
body:
The Northern Song ruled from Kaifeng until the Jurchen conquest of 1127 pushed the court south to Hangzhou. Advances in irrigation, printing, credit and shipbuilding supported dense cities, while Neo-Confucian philosophy reshaped Chinese thought.

More at [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Song_dynasty).

name: Avicenna and medieval medicine
summary: The Persian polymath wrote the *Canon of Medicine*, a medical text that was the standard in both Islamic and Christian worlds for half a millennium.
body:
Part of [Islamic Golden Age](event:islamic-golden-age). Born near Bukhara and dying at Hamadan, Avicenna drew Greek, Indian and Islamic medicine into one system; the *Canon* was still taught in European universities in the 1600s.

More at [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Avicenna).

name: Neo-Confucianism in Song China
summary: Philosophers blended Confucian ethics with Buddhist and Daoist metaphysics, creating an ideology that shaped East Asian thought for centuries.
body:
Part of [Song Dynasty](event:song-dynasty). Zhu Xi synthesised these traditions into a unified philosophy of cosmic principle (*li*) that became the orthodox teaching throughout the Confucian world.

More at [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neo-Confucianism).

name: Chimú Empire
summary: A pre-Inca Peruvian empire famous for textiles, metalwork and a sophisticated road system that the Inca would inherit.
body:
The Chimú were masters of silver and gold work; their capital Chan Chan was the largest city in pre-Columbian South America. The Inca absorbed their technology and aesthetics.

More at [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chimor).

name: Norse reach North America
summary: Leif Erikson's people built a small settlement at L'Anse aux Meadows in Newfoundland, five centuries before Columbus.
body:
Part of [Viking Age](event:viking-age). Tree-ring dating of the timbers puts occupation precisely at 1021 CE. The colony lasted only a few years.

More at [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Norse_colonization_of_North_America).

name: Seljuk Empire
summary: Nomadic Turks from Central Asia conquered much of the Islamic world and Anatolia, becoming patrons of Persian culture and precipitators of the Crusades.
body:
At their height the Seljuk sultans ruled from Anatolia to Central Asia, governing through Persian bureaucrats from Isfahan while keeping the Abbasid caliph in Baghdad as a figurehead. Their victory at [Manzikert](event:manzikert) alarmed Byzantium, whose appeal for help helped prompt [the Crusades](event:crusades).

More at [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seljuk_Empire).

name: Cahokia mound city
summary: In the Mississippi valley near present-day St. Louis, a Mississippian city rose and fell, leaving massive earthen mounds and mysteries.
body:
At its peak around 1100 CE, Cahokia may have held 10,000–20,000 residents, comparable to the largest European cities of the day. Its gradual abandonment is not fully explained; climate stress, resource depletion and political fragmentation have all been proposed.

More at [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cahokia).

name: East–West Schism
summary: Mutual excommunications formalised the split between the Catholic and Orthodox churches.
body:
Mutual excommunications formalised the split between the Catholic and Orthodox churches.

More at [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/East–West_Schism).

name: Al-Ghazali and Islamic theology
summary: The Persian theologian absorbed Greek logic into Islamic scholarship while attacking the metaphysics of the philosophers, reshaping Sunni thought for centuries.
body:
Part of [Islamic Golden Age](event:islamic-golden-age). His *Incoherence of the Philosophers* challenged Avicennan metaphysics, while his synthesis of law, theology and Sufism became mainstream Sunni teaching. The autobiography describing his crisis of doubt is a classic of spiritual literature.

More at [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Al-Ghazali).

name: Norman conquest of England
summary: William of Normandy defeated Harold at Hastings and took the English throne.
body:
The conquest replaced the English aristocracy wholesale, poured French vocabulary into the language, and produced the Domesday Book — the most detailed survey of any medieval kingdom.

More at [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Norman_Conquest).

name: Battle of Manzikert
summary: The Byzantine emperor was defeated by the Seljuk Turks, allowing them to settle Anatolia and eventually found an empire.
body:
The defeat opened the Anatolian plateau to Turkish settlement and began the slow displacement of the Greeks — a process that culminated in the [fall of Constantinople](event:fall-constantinople) nearly four centuries later.

More at [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_Manzikert).

name: Domesday Book
summary: William I's vast survey of England, recording land and taxes for every village — the most detailed census of any medieval kingdom.
body:
Part of [Norman conquest of England](event:hastings). Commissioners recorded holdings, ploughs and tenants shire by shire; the returns let William assess what he had conquered and tax it.

More at [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Domesday_Book).

name: First universities
summary: Bologna, then Paris and Oxford, organised teachers and students into self-governing corporations.
body:
Bologna, then Paris and Oxford, organised teachers and students into self-governing corporations.

More at [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Bologna).

name: The Crusades
summary: Two centuries of religious warfare between Latin Christendom and the Muslim states of the Levant.
body:
Urban II's call at Clermont launched the [First Crusade](event:first-crusade), which took Jerusalem in 1099. Later expeditions achieved less; the [Fourth](event:fourth-crusade) sacked Christian Constantinople instead, and the last mainland stronghold fell at [Acre](event:acre-1291).

The wars deepened contact — and enmity — between Europe and the Islamic world, and brought Arabic learning and goods westward.

More at [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crusades).

name: First Crusade
summary: A Latin army marched across Anatolia and took Jerusalem after a five-week siege, massacring much of its population.
body:
Part of [The Crusades](event:crusades). A Latin army marched across Anatolia and took Jerusalem after a five-week siege, massacring much of its population.

More at [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First_Crusade).

name: Great Zimbabwe
summary: A Bantu city-state built monumental stone walls and controlled gold and ivory trade with the Indian Ocean world.
body:
Its stone enclosures were built without mortar by Shona builders, and gold and ivory passed from here to Swahili ports on the Indian Ocean. The reasons for its decline are debated: exhausted soils and pasture, shifting trade routes and political fragmentation are all proposed.

More at [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Great_Zimbabwe).

name: Venetian–Genoese rivalry
summary: Two Italian maritime republics fought for control of Mediterranean and Black Sea trade, developing banking, double-entry accounting and marine insurance along the way.
body:
Genoese and Venetian galleys competed for the routes to Alexandria, the Levant and the Black Sea, fighting four wars between 1256 and 1381. Their commercial techniques, from bills of exchange to insurance contracts, outlasted the rivalry itself.

More at [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Venetian%E2%80%93Genoese_wars).

name: Angkor Wat built
summary: The Khmer kings raised the largest religious monument in the world, first Hindu and later Buddhist.
body:
The Khmer kings raised the largest religious monument in the world, first Hindu and later Buddhist.

More at [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angkor_Wat).

name: Knights Templar
summary: A military-monastic order founded to protect pilgrims and wage crusade; they became bankers and landholders across Christendom.
body:
Part of [The Crusades](event:crusades). Founded to guard pilgrims to Jerusalem, the Templars grew into landholders and lenders across Christendom. Philip IV of France, deeply in their debt, had the French brothers arrested in 1307; Pope Clement V dissolved the order in 1312.

More at [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Knights_Templar).

name: Zagwe dynasty in Ethiopia
summary: After Aksum's decline, Christian rule shifted to the Ethiopian highlands under the Zagwe kings, who cut the rock-hewn churches of Lalibela.
body:
The Zagwe, and after 1270 the Solomonic dynasty, held a Christian kingdom in the highlands while Islam spread along the coast and lowlands. The Ethiopian Orthodox church that resulted has survived to the present day.

More at [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zagwe_dynasty).

name: Saladin and the crusader wars
summary: The Kurdish general unified the Islamic world against the crusaders, retaking Jerusalem and establishing a new dynasty.
body:
Part of [The Crusades](event:crusades). Saladin's defeat of the Crusaders at Hattin in 1187 and the recovery of Jerusalem made him a legendary figure in both Islamic and Western tradition.

More at [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saladin).

name: Kamakura shogunate
summary: Military rule by the shoguns began; the samurai code and Zen Buddhism took root, transforming Japanese culture.
body:
Minamoto no Yoritomo established a warrior government at Kamakura while the emperor remained in Kyoto. Warrior families became the ruling class, Zen Buddhism took root, and the shogunate twice repelled Mongol invasions before falling in 1333.

More at [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kamakura_shogunate).

name: Decline of the Khmer Empire
summary: The Khmer empire that built Angkor gradually abandoned it, amid drought, war with Ayutthaya and a shift of power downriver.
body:
Tree-ring records show severe droughts alternating with heavy monsoons in the 14th and 15th centuries, straining the waterworks that fed [Angkor](event:angkor-wat). After the Siamese sack of 1431 the Khmer court moved toward Phnom Penh, and monks kept the temples.

More at [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Khmer_Empire).

name: Scholasticism peaks
summary: Medieval philosophers at universities used logic to reconcile faith and reason, culminating in the great systems of Aquinas and Duns Scotus.
body:
Working in the new universities, Aquinas, Albertus Magnus and Duns Scotus applied Aristotelian logic to Christian doctrine. The disputation method they refined shaped European teaching long after their metaphysics fell out of favour.

More at [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scholasticism).

name: Fourth Crusade sacks Constantinople
summary: Diverted by Venetian debts and dynastic politics, the crusaders stormed and looted the greatest Christian city in the world.
body:
Part of [The Crusades](event:crusades). Byzantium never fully recovered, which made the [fall of the city](event:fall-constantinople) in 1453 far easier.

More at [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fourth_Crusade).

name: Mongol conquests
summary: The largest contiguous land empire in history was assembled in three generations, from Korea to Hungary.
body:
[Genghis Khan](event:genghis-khan) united the steppe tribes and turned them into a disciplined army of mounted archers; his sons and grandsons destroyed the Jin, Khwarazmian and Abbasid states — [Baghdad](event:baghdad-1258) in 1258 — and founded the [Yuan dynasty](event:yuan-dynasty) in China.

The destruction was immense, but the *Pax Mongolica* also made Eurasia briefly safe for travellers like [Marco Polo](event:marco-polo) — and for the [plague](event:black-death).

More at [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mongol_conquests).

name: Genghis Khan proclaimed
summary: Temüjin united the Mongol tribes and was acclaimed universal ruler at a kurultai on the Onon river.
body:
Part of [Mongol conquests](event:mongol-conquests). Temüjin united the Mongol tribes and was acclaimed universal ruler at a kurultai on the Onon river.

More at [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genghis_Khan).

name: Magna Carta
summary: English barons forced King John to accept written limits on royal power at Runnymede.
body:
Most of its clauses concerned feudal grievances, but the principle that the ruler is subject to law — and the promise of judgement by peers — was quoted for centuries afterwards, including by the framers of the [American constitution](event:us-constitution).

More at [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Magna_Carta).

name: Order of Preachers founded
summary: The Dominican friars were founded to preach against heresy and became a major intellectual force in the medieval Church.
body:
Dominic founded the order at Toulouse to preach against the Cathars; it grew into the leading teaching order of the medieval church, with Aquinas among its members. Dominicans also staffed much of the medieval Inquisition.

More at [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dominican_Order).

name: Mali Empire
summary: West African kingdom that controlled the trans-Saharan gold trade, making Timbuktu a centre of Islamic learning.
body:
Sundiata Keita united the Mandé chiefdoms in the 13th century, and the empire grew rich on the gold of Bambuk and Bure and the salt of the Sahara. [Mansa Musa's pilgrimage](event:mansa-musa) put Mali on European maps, and Timbuktu became a centre of Islamic scholarship before Songhai took its place.

More at [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mali_Empire).

name: Sukhothai Kingdom
summary: A Thai kingdom in the north produced a distinctive art style and pioneered Thai writing, which survives today.
body:
Sukhothai's bronze Buddhas and celadon ware are among Southeast Asia's finest, and an inscription attributed to King Ramkhamhaeng is the earliest known Thai script. The kingdom was absorbed by Ayutthaya in the 15th century.

More at [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sukhothai_Kingdom).

name: Mongol sack of Baghdad
summary: Hulagu's army destroyed the Abbasid capital, killed the caliph and ended the [Islamic Golden Age](event:islamic-golden-age) in Iraq.
body:
Part of [Mongol conquests](event:mongol-conquests). Hulagu's army destroyed the Abbasid capital, killed the caliph and ended the [Islamic Golden Age](event:islamic-golden-age) in Iraq.

More at [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Siege_of_Baghdad_(1258)).

name: Yuan dynasty founded
summary: Kublai Khan completed the conquest of Song China and ruled it as a Chinese emperor from Dadu, modern Beijing.
body:
Part of [Mongol conquests](event:mongol-conquests). Kublai Khan completed the conquest of Song China and ruled it as a Chinese emperor from Dadu, modern Beijing.

More at [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yuan_dynasty).

name: Travels of Marco Polo
summary: A Venetian merchant's account of twenty years in Asia became medieval Europe's window on China.
body:
Part of [Mongol conquests](event:mongol-conquests). The book was widely doubted, and widely read — [Columbus](event:columbus) owned an annotated copy.

More at [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marco_Polo).

name: Fall of Acre
summary: The last crusader stronghold on the Levantine mainland fell to the Mamluks.
body:
Part of [The Crusades](event:crusades). The last crusader stronghold on the Levantine mainland fell to the Mamluks.

More at [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Siege_of_Acre_(1291)).

name: Majapahit Empire
summary: A Javanese maritime power dominated much of the Indonesian archipelago, drawing tribute and trade from ports across the Java Sea.
body:
At its height under Hayam Wuruk and the minister Gajah Mada, Majapahit claimed authority over ports from Sumatra to the Moluccas. Its literature, law and Hindu-Buddhist art shaped Javanese culture long after the empire fragmented.

More at [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Majapahit).

name: Ottoman Empire
summary: From a frontier beylik in Anatolia the Ottomans built an empire spanning the Balkans, the Middle East and North Africa for six centuries.
body:
Its high point came under Suleiman the Magnificent; its collapse after [the First World War](event:ww1) created the modern map of the Middle East.

More at [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ottoman_Empire).

name: Little Ice Age
summary: A few tenths of a degree of cooling brought advancing glaciers, frozen rivers and repeated harvest failures across the northern hemisphere.
body:
Solar minima, volcanic eruptions and possibly American [reforestation after depopulation](event:americas-epidemics) all contributed. The Thames froze hard enough for frost fairs; Norse Greenland was abandoned.

More at [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Little_Ice_Age).

name: Mansa Musa's pilgrimage to Mecca
summary: The ruler of Mali crossed the Sahara with so much gold that he depressed its price in Cairo for years.
body:
Mali's wealth put Timbuktu on European maps and made it a centre of Islamic scholarship.

More at [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mansa_Musa).

name: Tenochtitlan founded
summary: The Aztecs built their capital on an island in Lake Texcoco, constructing one of the largest cities in the world.
body:
Mexica tradition holds that the city was founded where an eagle perched on a cactus, the sign promised by their god. Built on an island in Lake Texcoco and extended with causeways and chinampas, it became the capital of the [Aztec Empire](event:aztec-empire) and, by 1500, one of the largest cities in the world.

More at [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tenochtitlan).

name: Hundred Years' War
summary: England and France fought intermittently for 116 years over the French crown.
body:
Longbows won [Crécy](event:crecy) and [Agincourt](event:agincourt), but France recovered under [Joan of Arc](event:joan-of-arc) and, with gunpowder artillery, expelled the English from all but Calais.

More at [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hundred_Years%27_War).

name: Alhambra Palace
summary: The last Muslim emirs of Granada built a palace of extraordinary beauty, blending Islamic and Spanish architectural traditions.
body:
Part of [The Reconquista](event:reconquista). The Alhambra's stucco work, calligraphy and water features represent the peak of Islamic art in medieval Europe before its conquest in 1492.

More at [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alhambra).

name: Black Death
summary: The deadliest pandemic in recorded history killed an estimated third to half of Europe's population in six years.
body:
Plague travelled west along [Silk Road](event:silk-road) and Genoese trade routes, reaching Sicily in 1347 and Scandinavia by 1350. Contemporaries had no idea what caused it; the bacterium *Yersinia pestis* was identified only in 1894.

The survivors inherited a labour shortage that broke serfdom in much of western Europe, raised wages, and shook the authority of the Church — conditions in which the [Renaissance](event:renaissance) took root.

More at [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Death).

name: Battle of Crécy
summary: English longbowmen destroyed the French cavalry, an early sign that armoured knights were losing their dominance.
body:
Part of [Hundred Years' War](event:hundred-years-war). English longbowmen destroyed the French cavalry, an early sign that armoured knights were losing their dominance.

More at [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_Crécy).

name: Duchy of Burgundy at its height
summary: A wealthy principality between France and the Holy Roman Empire, Burgundy became a centre of art, music and courtly culture.
body:
The dukes of Burgundy were patrons of the Early Flemish painters and musicians. The duchy fell to France when its last duke died without a male heir.

More at [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Duchy_of_Burgundy).

name: Ming dynasty
summary: Native Chinese rule was restored after the Mongols; the Forbidden City was built and the [Great Wall](event:great-wall) rebuilt in the form seen today.
body:
Native Chinese rule was restored after the Mongols; the Forbidden City was built and the [Great Wall](event:great-wall) rebuilt in the form seen today.

More at [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ming_dynasty).

name: Metal movable type in Korea
summary: Korean foundries cast movable metal type; the Jikji of 1377 is the oldest surviving book printed with it, decades before Gutenberg.
body:
Woodblock printing came from China, but Goryeo craftsmen cast type in bronze. Records describe metal-type printing as early as 1234, and the surviving *Jikji* was printed at Cheongju in 1377. Joseon foundries continued the technique, though it never displaced woodblocks for long print runs.

More at [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jikji).

name: Medici banking and political power
summary: The Medici family's banking innovations and patronage of the arts made them the de facto rulers of Florence and arbiters of Renaissance taste.
body:
Cosimo and later Lorenzo the Magnificent turned banking wealth into political control of Florence and into patronage: Brunelleschi and Donatello worked for the early Medici, Botticelli and the young Michelangelo for Lorenzo. The bank itself collapsed shortly before the family's expulsion in 1494.

More at [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/House_of_Medici).

name: The Renaissance
summary: A revival of classical learning and a transformation of European art, architecture and thought, beginning in Florence.
body:
Perspective, anatomy, humanist scholarship and patronage by bankers and popes produced [Leonardo](event:mona-lisa), [Michelangelo](event:sistine-chapel), Raphael and Brunelleschi's dome.

The recovery of Greek texts — accelerated by scholars fleeing the [fall of Constantinople](event:fall-constantinople) — and cheap books from the [printing press](event:printing-press) spread the movement across Europe.

More at [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Renaissance).

name: Voyages of Zheng He
summary: Chinese treasure fleets of hundreds of ships sailed to India, Arabia and East Africa decades before the Portuguese.
body:
Part of [Ming dynasty](event:ming-dynasty). The largest ships dwarfed anything in Europe. After 1433 the voyages were halted and the records suppressed — one of history's great counterfactuals.

More at [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ming_treasure_voyages).

name: Forbidden City built
summary: The Ming emperor built a massive palace complex at the heart of Beijing, its layout mirroring cosmic order and containing nearly 1,000 buildings.
body:
Part of [Ming dynasty](event:ming-dynasty). The Forbidden City was closed to commoners for five centuries and is now a museum of imperial life.

More at [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Forbidden_City).

name: Battle of Agincourt
summary: Henry V's outnumbered and exhausted army routed the French in a muddy defile.
body:
Part of [Hundred Years' War](event:hundred-years-war). Henry V's outnumbered and exhausted army routed the French in a muddy defile.

More at [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_Agincourt).

name: Age of Discovery
summary: European ships opened sea routes to Africa, Asia and the Americas, joining the world's hemispheres into a single system.
body:
Portuguese caravels worked their way down the African coast for decades before [Dias](event:dias) rounded the Cape and [da Gama](event:da-gama) reached India. [Columbus](event:columbus) sailed west and found a continent nobody in Europe expected; [Magellan's expedition](event:magellan) went all the way round.

What followed was the [Columbian Exchange](event:columbian-exchange), the [conquest of the Americas](event:spanish-conquest) and the [Atlantic slave trade](event:slave-trade) — the beginning of a genuinely global economy, built on immense violence.

More at [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Age_of_Discovery).

name: Prince Henry the Navigator
summary: The Portuguese prince sponsored voyages down the Atlantic coast of Africa and the settlement of Madeira and the Azores.
body:
Part of [Age of Discovery](event:age-of-discovery). Henry's captains passed Cape Bojador in 1434 and reached Sierra Leone by his death, bringing back gold, and enslaved Africans whose trade Portugal would expand for centuries. The caravel and improved navigation developed under his patronage made the later routes to India possible.

More at [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prince_Henry_the_Navigator).

name: Aztec Empire
summary: The Triple Alliance ruled central Mexico from Tenochtitlan, a lake city of perhaps 200,000 people.
body:
The Triple Alliance ruled central Mexico from Tenochtitlan, a lake city of perhaps 200,000 people.

More at [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aztec_Empire).

name: Joan of Arc
summary: A peasant girl claiming divine voices lifted the siege of Orléans and had the dauphin crowned at Reims; she was burned as a heretic two years later.
body:
Part of [Hundred Years' War](event:hundred-years-war). A peasant girl claiming divine voices lifted the siege of Orléans and had the dauphin crowned at Reims; she was burned as a heretic two years later.

More at [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joan_of_Arc).

name: Inca Empire
summary: Tawantinsuyu stretched 4,000 km along the Andes, bound by roads, terraces and knotted-string records, without wheels or writing.
body:
Tawantinsuyu stretched 4,000 km along the Andes, bound by roads, terraces and knotted-string records, without wheels or writing.

More at [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inca_Empire).

name: Gutenberg's printing press
summary: Movable metal type made books cheap, and made it impossible to suppress an idea once it had spread.
body:
Gutenberg combined a wine-press, oil-based ink and a mould for casting reusable type. By 1500 Europe held perhaps twenty million printed books, more than scribes had produced in the preceding thousand years.

The press carried the [Reformation](event:reformation), the [Scientific Revolution](event:copernicus) and eventually mass literacy.

More at [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Printing_press).

name: Pope Nicholas V and the early Renaissance
summary: The pope patronised humanists, collected manuscripts and began rebuilding St. Peter's Basilica, making Rome a centre of the Renaissance.
body:
Part of [The Renaissance](event:renaissance). Nicholas bought and copied Greek and Latin manuscripts on a scale no one had attempted, founding the collection that became the Vatican Library, and began the rebuilding of St Peter's.

More at [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope_Nicholas_V).

name: Fall of Constantinople
summary: Ottoman cannon breached the Theodosian walls and the last Roman emperor died fighting; the Byzantine Empire ended after 1,100 years.
body:
Mehmed II made the city his capital and Hagia Sophia a mosque. Greek scholars fled west with their manuscripts, feeding the [Renaissance](event:renaissance), while Ottoman control of the eastern trade routes sharpened European interest in finding a [sea route to Asia](event:age-of-discovery).

More at [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fall_of_Constantinople).

name: Gutenberg Bible
summary: The first major book printed with movable type was a Latin Bible, made in Mainz in an edition of about 180 copies.
body:
Part of [Gutenberg's printing press](event:printing-press). The 42-line Bible demonstrated that printing was economically viable and could match handwritten books in quality.

More at [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gutenberg_Bible).

name: Songhai Empire
summary: The successor to Mali, Songhai became the largest empire in medieval West Africa before being conquered by Morocco.
body:
Sunni Ali took Timbuktu and Djenné from the declining Mali, and Askia Muhammad extended the empire to its greatest reach. Its defeat by a Moroccan expedition armed with firearms in 1591 broke the last of the great Sahelian empires.

More at [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Songhai_Empire).

name: Dias rounds the Cape of Good Hope
summary: Bartolomeu Dias proved that the Atlantic and Indian oceans connect.
body:
Part of [Age of Discovery](event:age-of-discovery). Bartolomeu Dias proved that the Atlantic and Indian oceans connect.

More at [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bartolomeu_Dias).

name: Fall of Granada
summary: The last Muslim emirate in Spain surrendered to Ferdinand and Isabella; Jews were expelled from Spain the same year.
body:
Part of [The Reconquista](event:reconquista). The last Muslim emirate in Spain surrendered to Ferdinand and Isabella; Jews were expelled from Spain the same year.

More at [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Granada_War).

name: Columbus reaches the Americas
summary: Three Spanish ships made landfall in the Bahamas, beginning sustained contact between the Old World and the New.
body:
Part of [Age of Discovery](event:age-of-discovery). Columbus was looking for Asia and died insisting he had found it. The consequences — [the Columbian Exchange](event:columbian-exchange), the collapse of Indigenous populations under [epidemic disease](event:americas-epidemics), and centuries of colonisation — were world-historical and, for the Americas, catastrophic.

More at [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Voyages_of_Christopher_Columbus).

name: The Columbian Exchange
summary: Crops, animals and diseases moved between hemispheres, transforming diets and populations on every continent.
body:
Maize, potatoes, tomatoes, cassava, chillies and tobacco went east; wheat, sugar, horses, cattle and — devastatingly — [smallpox and measles](event:americas-epidemics) went west.

The potato and maize eventually supported large population growth in Europe, Africa and China; the exchange is one reason the world could feed the [Industrial Revolution](event:industrial-revolution).

More at [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Columbian_exchange).

name: Treaty of Tordesillas
summary: Spain and Portugal drew a line across the world, dividing newly discovered lands between them.
body:
Negotiated directly between the two crowns to revise an earlier papal bull, the treaty drew a meridian 370 leagues west of the Cape Verde islands: land found east of it fell to Portugal, west of it to Spain. The line later gave Portugal its claim to Brazil.

No other European power accepted the division for long, and none of the peoples living in the lands concerned were consulted.

More at [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Treaty_of_Tordesillas).

name: Vasco da Gama reaches India
summary: The first sea route from Europe to India broke the Venetian and Ottoman monopoly on the spice trade.
body:
Part of [Age of Discovery](event:age-of-discovery). The first sea route from Europe to India broke the Venetian and Ottoman monopoly on the spice trade.

More at [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vasco_da_Gama).
